body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), \[d_P=P(R=C\mid X=c_P),\qquad y_P=E_P[(Y(1)-Y(0))\mathbf 1\{R=C\}\mid X=c_P],\] and therefore \(\theta_P=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_P]\).
body.justification: This fixes the causal interpretation before the statistical nonregularity is analyzed.
body.gap: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) give the known-cutoff Wald identification argument; the proposition records the same argument on the preserved unknown-cutoff triangular class.
body.consumer: Every later confidence interval can be interpreted as an interval for the local complier causal effect rather than only for an observable jump ratio.
